cards.title: Prepositions: quick review
cards.body: Prepositions show place (under, behind, between, among) and time (at noon, on Monday, in July, during, since, for). A prepositional phrase is the preposition + its noun: behind the old shed. The subject is never inside the phrase. Comma after a phrase that starts a sentence.

cards.title: Conjunctions: quick review
cards.body: FANBOYS (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so) join equal ideas; comma before them when they join two complete sentences. Subordinating conjunctions (because, although, when, if, unless…) start a part that can’t stand alone; comma after it when it comes first. Pairs: both… and, either… or, neither… nor, not only… but also.

cards.title: How the check works
cards.body: First, a 10-question quiz: you need 8 right (80%) to pass. If you don’t pass, you’ll see which skills to review, and you’ll get new questions next time. Then you’ll write a short paragraph that shows off everything you’ve learned. Quill gives it a score.
